subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared filename decoder live, and which channel filename paths must be migrated before this issue can close?
rationale: Repository policy keeps core lean and plugin-safe, while current code has separate core and Feishu parsers and the open implementation PR is partial, so automation should not choose the permanent API boundary alone.

options.title: Media-core shared helper
options.body: Put the decoder in packages/media-core or an SDK-exposed media boundary, then migrate remote media and Feishu filename paths through it before closing this issue.

options.title: Narrow Feishu-only handling
options.body: Keep the existing Feishu-local recovery and close only narrower Feishu bugs, leaving this broader shared decoder request open or explicitly deferred.

options.title: Defer broad migration
options.body: Wait for another non-Feishu channel to show concrete filename corruption before expanding the shared decoder surface.

recommendation.title: Media-core shared helper
recommendation.body: Put the decoder in packages/media-core or an SDK-exposed media boundary, then migrate remote media and Feishu filename paths through it before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice primarily affects the current remote-media helper and media-core/plugin-safe boundary that @steipete introduced and recently maintained.
